newsitem.title: USA: Sandler says sees positives in Phila. school bonds.
newsitem.headline: Sandler says sees positives in Phila. school bonds.

text.p: A recent court ruling has given a positive spin to the Philadelphia School District's credit outlook, Sandler O'Neill & Partners LP said Monday, in adding the district to its Watch List of municipal bonds.
In its analysis of the district, Sandler noted a recent Commonwealth Court ruling concluded that the state must participate in the funding of desegregation in Philadelphia schools.

"While the state Supreme Court will ultimately decide if the state will be obligated to make the payment, the lower court ruling indicates that there may be the potential for new financial assistance for the school district," the report said.

The state Supreme Court has since taken over the case, and said the lower court's ruling will be considered advisory only. But Sandler said the lower court's ruling was based on existing Supreme Court precedent, so the potential exists for a favorable ruling from the higher court as well.
Sandler noted that the school district has been hindered by a difficult fiscal environment, but said a "creative and aggressive management" has maintained fiscal balance.
In addition, Pennsylvania has a state intercept mechanism which benefits the school district's bonds, Sandler said.

Moody's Investors Service does not recognize the intercept, because of timing and sufficiency concerns. But Sandler said it disagrees with Moody's position since it gives no weight to the ability of management to deal with such problems as they arise.
